1.q: הַ⁠דָּבָר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הָיָ֣ה אֶֽל יִרְמְיָ֔הוּ מֵ⁠אֵ֥ת יְהוָ֖ה
1.note: Jeremiah is using **The word that was to Jeremiah from Yahweh** as a common expression of the culture to mean “Yahweh gave a message to Jeremiah.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [This is the message that Yahweh spoke to Jeremiah]

2.note: Here Yahweh is speaking of the temple as his **house**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [at the gate of the temple of Yahweh]

2.q: וְ⁠אָמַרְתָּ֞ שִׁמְע֣וּ דְבַר יְהוָ֗ה כָּל יְהוּדָה֙ הַ⁠בָּאִים֙ בַּ⁠שְּׁעָרִ֣ים הָ⁠אֵ֔לֶּה לְ⁠הִֽשְׁתַּחֲוֺ֖ת לַ⁠יהוָֽה
2.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [And you shall tell all of Judah, who enter these gates to bow down to Yahweh, to hear the word of Yahweh]

In this verse, the word **Judah** is singular in form, but it refers to all the people of that nation as a group. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use the plural form of “Judah.” Alternate translation: [all of you people of Judah, who enter these gates]

3.note: Here Yahweh is speaking as if the conduct of these people were the **ways** on which they walk. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Make your conduct and your actions good]

This is the beginning of what Jeremiah said as he delivered Yahweh’s message. You may wish to mark the words of this speech with a first-level quotation mark at the beginning and end of them or with some other punctuation or convention that your language uses to indicate a first-level quotation. Alternate translation: [ So says the Lord God Almighty]

4.note: Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe **words** that are characterized by **deceit**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [in deceitful words]

4.q: לֵ⁠אמֹ֑ר הֵיכַ֤ל יְהוָה֙ הֵיכַ֣ל יְהוָ֔ה הֵיכַ֥ל יְהוָ֖ה
4.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [saying that the temple of Yahweh, the temple of Yahweh, the temple of Yahweh]

4.q: הֵיכַ֤ל יְהוָה֙ הֵיכַ֣ל יְהוָ֔ה הֵיכַ֥ל יְהוָ֖ה
4.note: The people are repeating the phrase **The temple of Yahweh** in order to intensify their expression of the idea that it conveys. If your language can repeat words for intensification, it would be appropriate to do that here in your translation. If not, your language may have another way of expressing the intensification. Alternate translation: [The very temple of Yahweh]

The implication is that the people believe that the presence of Yahweh’s **temple** among them guarantees that they will be safe, no matter how they behave. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [This is the temple of Yahweh, so nothing bad can happen to us]

5.q: כִּ֤י אִם הֵיטֵיב֙ תֵּיטִ֔יבוּ אֶת דַּרְכֵי⁠כֶ֖ם וְ⁠אֶת מַֽעַלְלֵי⁠כֶ֑ם
5.note: Yahweh is presenting a possible condition, that he will allow the people of Judah to remain in this place only if they change their conduct and act justly. Use a natural form in your language for introducing a condition that could happen. Alternate translation: [For only if you truly change your ways and your deeds]

5.q: אִם הֵיטֵיב֙ תֵּיטִ֔יבוּ אֶת דַּרְכֵי⁠כֶ֖ם וְ⁠אֶת מַֽעַלְלֵי⁠כֶ֑ם אִם עָשׂ֤וֹ תַֽעֲשׂוּ֙ מִשְׁפָּ֔ט
5.note: Yahweh is repeating forms of the verbs **make good** and **do** in order to intensify his expression of the ideas that they convey. If your language can repeat words for intensification, it would be appropriate to do that here in your translation. If not, your language may have another way of expressing the intensification. Alternate translation: [if you thoroughly make good your ways and your deeds, if you certainly do justice]

Yahweh is not referring to a specific **man** or a specific **neighbor**. He means any two people in general. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [between one person and another person]

6.note: Yahweh is not referring to a specific **stranger**, a specific **fatherless one**, or a specific **widow**. He means people in each of these situations in general. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [if you do not oppress strangers, fatherless ones, or widows]

Yahweh is using **innocent blood** to represent innocent people who are killed. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression from your culture or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and you do not kill innocent people]

Yahweh is using **walk after** as a common expression of the culture to mean “worship.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and do not serve other gods]

7.note: Here Yahweh is speaking as if the ancestors of these people were their **fathers**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [to your forefathers]

Yahweh is using **from ancient times and to eternity** as a common expression of the culture to mean “for all time.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [for all time]

8.note: Jeremiah is using the term **Behold** to focus his listeners’ attention on what he is about to say. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation. Alternate translation: [Look]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **deceit**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [deceitful words]

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **benefit**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [and they do not benefit you at all] or [and they are not helpful to you]

9.q: הֲ⁠גָנֹ֤ב רָצֹ֨חַ֙ וְֽ⁠נָאֹ֔ף וְ⁠הִשָּׁבֵ֥עַ לַ⁠שֶּׁ֖קֶר וְ⁠קַטֵּ֣ר לַ⁠בָּ֑עַל וְ⁠הָלֹ֗ךְ אַחֲרֵ֛י אֱלֹהִ֥ים אֲחֵרִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹֽא יְדַעְתֶּֽם
9.note: Yahweh is using the question form to rebuke the people of Judah for the wicked things they are doing. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [It is shameful that you steal, murder, and commit adultery and swear deceitfully and burn incense to Baal and walk after other gods whom you have not known]

10.note: Here, **my face** represents the presence of Yahweh. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [and stand in my presence]

The expression **is called by my name** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [which people call by my name]

Yahweh is using **which my name is called over** as a common expression of the culture to mean “belonging to me.” In that culture if someone called something by their name they were claiming ownership over it. If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [which is the place that I have claimed as belonging to me] or [which is known as belonging to me]
If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [and say that you are delivered]

The expression **We are delivered** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [Yahweh has rescued us]
Yahweh is speaking of his temple as if it were a **house**. Alternate translation: [my temple]

11.q: הַ⁠מְעָרַ֣ת פָּרִצִ֗ים הָיָ֨ה הַ⁠בַּ֧יִת הַ⁠זֶּ֛ה אֲשֶׁר נִקְרָֽא שְׁמִ֥⁠י עָלָ֖י⁠ו בְּ⁠עֵינֵי⁠כֶ֑ם
11.note: Yahweh is using the question form to rebuke the people of Judah for treating his temple as a safe hideout from which they can go out and do wicked things. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [This house, which is called by my name, has become a cave of robbers in your eyes!]

11.q: הַ⁠מְעָרַ֣ת פָּרִצִ֗ים הָיָ֨ה הַ⁠בַּ֧יִת הַ⁠זֶּ֛ה אֲשֶׁר נִקְרָֽא שְׁמִ֥⁠י
11.note: Here Yahweh is speaking as if the temple were a **cave of robbers**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Has this house, which is called by my name, become a hiding place for criminals]

Yahweh is using **in your eyes** as a common expression of the culture to mean “in your own estimation.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [in your own opinion]

Jeremiah is using the term **behold** to focus his listeners’ attention on what he is about to say. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation. Alternate translation: [Be aware]

Jeremiah is using **the declaration of Yahweh** to indicate that what has been said is a direct quotation from Yahweh and comes with Yahweh’s authority. In your translation, use a natural way of indicating direct quotations in your language.
See how you translated this same phrase in 7:10.

12.q: כִּ֣י לְכוּ נָ֗א אֶל מְקוֹמִ⁠י֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּ⁠שִׁיל֔וֹ אֲשֶׁ֨ר שִׁכַּ֧נְתִּֽי שְׁמִ֛⁠י שָׁ֖ם בָּ⁠רִֽאשׁוֹנָ֑ה וּ⁠רְאוּ֙ אֵ֣ת אֲשֶׁר עָשִׂ֣יתִי ל֔⁠וֹ
12.note: The implication is that Yahweh destroyed the sanctuary that had been at **Shiloh** because of the wicked things his people did there. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [But go now to my place that was in Shiloh, where I made my name dwell in the beginning, and see how I destroyed it]
Here, **my name** represents Yahweh himself. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [where I myself first dwelled]

13.q: יַ֧עַן עֲשׂוֹתְ⁠כֶ֛ם אֶת כָּל הַ⁠מַּֽעֲשִׂ֥ים הָ⁠אֵ֖לֶּה
13.note: The word translated as **on account of** indicates that what follows is a reason for the result that Yahweh states in the next verse. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a reason. Alternate translation: [So now, since you did all of these deeds]
See how you translated the similar expression in 7:11.

Yahweh is using **rising early and speaking** as a common expression of the culture to mean “speaking to you persistently.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [again and again]

14.note: Yahweh is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [therefore I shall do the same thing to the house]
See how you translated this same phrase in 7:10.

15.note: Here, **my face** represents the presence of Yahweh. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [And I shall cast you out from where I am]

Here Yahweh is speaking as if the fellow Israelites of these people were their **brothers**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [all your fellow Israelites]

Here Yahweh is speaking as if the descendants of Ephraim were his **seed**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [all the offspring of Ephraim]

16.q: וְ⁠אַתָּ֞ה אַל תִּתְפַּלֵּ֣ל בְּעַד הָ⁠עָ֣ם הַ⁠זֶּ֗ה
16.note: The word **you** is singular here because Yahweh is addressing Jeremiah individually, so use the singular form in your translation if your language marks that distinction.

Yahweh is using **lift up** as a common expression of the culture to mean “utter aloud.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and do not cry out or pray aloud for them]

Yahweh is using **hear** as a common expression of the culture to mean “grant what is requested.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [for I shall not grant what you ask]

17.q: הַֽ⁠אֵינְ⁠ךָ֣ רֹאֶ֔ה מָ֛ה הֵ֥מָּה עֹשִׂ֖ים בְּ⁠עָרֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֑ה וּ⁠בְ⁠חֻצ֖וֹת יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם
17.note: Yahweh is using the question form to direct Jeremiah’s attention to what the people are doing. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [You surely see what they are doing in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem!]

18.note: This could mean: (1) the phrase marks provoking Yahweh to anger as the result of what these people are doing, even though it is not their purpose. Alternate translation: See the UST. (2) the phrase **in order to** marks provoking Yahweh to anger as the purpose for which these people are doing these things. Alternate translation: [deliberately provoking my anger]

Here the masculine term **sons** has a generic sense that includes both boys and girls. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use language in your translation that is clearly inclusive of both boys and girls. Alternate translation: [The children are collecting wood]

Yahweh is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [and the fathers are kindling the fire for them]
The phrase **the Queen of the Heavens** is the name of a goddess whom people of that time worshiped.

19.q: הַ⁠אֹתִ֛⁠י הֵ֥ם מַכְעִסִ֖ים נְאֻם יְהוָ֑ה הֲ⁠ל֣וֹא אֹתָ֔⁠ם לְמַ֖עַן בֹּ֥שֶׁת פְּנֵי⁠הֶֽם
19.note: Yahweh is using the question form to emphasize that these people are not harming him but are harming themselves. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate these questions as statements or as exclamations. Alternate translation: [They are not provoking me to anger”—the declaration of Yahweh—“but themselves, to the shame of their own faces!]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **shame**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [so that they themselves become ashamed]

Yahweh is using the phrase **to the shame of** their faces as a common expression of the culture to mean “to their own public disgrace.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [to their own public disgrace]

20.q: לָ⁠כֵ֞ן כֹּה אָמַ֣ר אֲדֹנָ֣⁠י יְהֹוִ֗ה הִנֵּ֨ה אַפִּ֤⁠י וַֽ⁠חֲמָתִ⁠י֙ נִתֶּ֨כֶת֙ אֶל הַ⁠מָּק֣וֹם הַ⁠זֶּ֔ה
20.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [Therefore, the Lord Yahweh says that his nose and his heat will be poured out on this place]

20.q: אַפִּ֤⁠י וַֽ⁠חֲמָתִ⁠י֙ נִתֶּ֨כֶת֙ אֶל הַ⁠מָּק֣וֹם הַ⁠זֶּ֔ה
20.note: The expression **will be poured out** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [I will pour out my nose and my heat on this place]

The terms **nose** and **heat** mean similar things. Yahweh is using the two terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [my furious anger]

Yahweh is using **my nose and my heat** as a common expression of the culture to mean “my anger.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [my blazing fury] or [my fierce anger]

Here Yahweh is speaking as if his anger were a liquid that could be **poured out**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [will come fully upon this place]

20.q: עַל הָֽ⁠אָדָם֙ וְ⁠עַל הַ⁠בְּהֵמָ֔ה וְ⁠עַל עֵ֥ץ הַ⁠שָּׂדֶ֖ה וְ⁠עַל פְּרִ֣י הָֽ⁠אֲדָמָ֑ה
20.note: Yahweh is referring to every living thing in the land by naming its major components, **man**, **beast**, **the tree of the field**, and **the fruit of the ground**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [on every living thing in the land]

Here Yahweh is speaking as if his anger were a fire that would **burn** and that no one could put out. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and my fury will keep raging and no one will be able to end it]

The expression **will not be quenched** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [and no one will be able to put it out]

21.q: עֹלוֹתֵי⁠כֶ֛ם סְפ֥וּ עַל זִבְחֵי⁠כֶ֖ם וְ⁠אִכְל֥וּ בָשָֽׂר
21.note: Yahweh actually means to communicate the opposite of the literal meaning of what he is saying here. If a speaker of your language would not do that, you could translate the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Your burnt offerings and your sacrifices mean nothing to me, so you may as well eat the meat yourselves]

22.q: לֹֽא דִבַּ֤רְתִּי אֶת אֲבֽוֹתֵי⁠כֶם֙ וְ⁠לֹ֣א צִוִּיתִ֔י⁠ם בְּ⁠י֛וֹם הוציא אוֹתָ֖⁠ם מֵ⁠אֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם עַל דִּבְרֵ֥י עוֹלָ֖ה וָ⁠זָֽבַח
22.note: Yahweh says **I did not speak to your fathers, nor did I command them** as an extreme statement for emphasis. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use a different way to express the emphasis. Alternate translation: [it was not primarily concerning matters of burnt offering and sacrifice that I spoke to your fathers and gave them commands on the day I brought them out from the land of Egypt]

Yahweh is using **on the day** as a common expression of the culture to mean “at the time.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [at the time I brought them out from the land of Egypt]

23.q: כִּ֣י אִֽם אֶת הַ⁠דָּבָ֣ר הַ֠⁠זֶּה צִוִּ֨יתִי אוֹתָ֤⁠ם לֵ⁠אמֹר֙ שִׁמְע֣וּ בְ⁠קוֹלִ֔⁠י וְ⁠הָיִ֤יתִי לָ⁠כֶם֙ לֵֽ⁠אלֹהִ֔ים וְ⁠אַתֶּ֖ם תִּֽהְיוּ לִ֣⁠י לְ⁠עָ֑ם
23.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [But I commanded them this word, telling them to listen to my voice, and that I would be their God and they would be my people, and that they should walk in all the ways that I commanded them so that it might go well for them]
Here, **my voice** represents what Yahweh commands. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [Obey what I command]

24.q: וְ⁠לֹ֤א שָֽׁמְעוּ֙ וְ⁠לֹֽא הִטּ֣וּ אֶת אָזְנָ֔⁠ם
24.note: The pronoun **they** refers to the ancestors of the people whom Yahweh is addressing. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [But your ancestors did not listen, and they did not incline their ear]

Yahweh is using **incline their ear** as a common expression of the culture to mean “pay attention.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and they did not pay attention]

Here Yahweh is speaking as if the way these people behaved were a path on which they **walked**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And they lived their lives following their own schemes]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **stubbornness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [as their stubborn and evil heart directed]

Here Yahweh is speaking as if the thoughts and desires of these people were located in their **heart**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [in accordance with their stubborn and evil desires]

Yahweh is using **to the back and not to the face** as a common expression of the culture to mean “backward and not forward.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and they went backward and not forward]

25.note: By **your fathers went out from the land of Egypt**, Yahweh means the day when he brought the Israelites out of Egypt where they had been slaves. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [your ancestors left the land of Egypt, where they had been slaves]

26.note: The pronoun **they** could refer to: (1) the people of Judah whom Yahweh is addressing here. Alternate translation: See the UST or (2) the ancestors whom Yahweh has been describing in the previous verses. Alternate translation: [And yet those ancestors did not listen to me]

Yahweh is using **stiffened their neck** as a common expression of the culture to mean “became stubborn.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [but they became stubborn]

Yahweh is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [They did evil more than their fathers did evil]

27.q: וְ⁠דִבַּרְתָּ֤ אֲלֵי⁠הֶם֙ אֶת כָּל הַ⁠דְּבָרִ֣ים הָ⁠אֵ֔לֶּה
27.note: The word **you** is singular here because Yahweh is addressing Jeremiah individually, so use the singular form in your translation if your language marks that distinction.

28.q: וְ⁠אָמַרְתָּ֣ אֲלֵי⁠הֶ֗ם זֶ֤ה הַ⁠גּוֹי֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לֽוֹא שָׁמְע֗וּ בְּ⁠קוֹל֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהָ֔י⁠ו
28.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [And you shall tell them that they are the nation that does not listen to the voice of Yahweh their God]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **discipline**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [and refuses to be corrected]

Yahweh is speaking of **Truth** as if it were a living thing that could die. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [That which is true is completely gone]

The expression **has been cut off** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [and they have cut it off from their mouth]

Here, **their mouth** represents what these people say. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [and no longer comes from what they say]

In this verse, the word **mouth** is singular in form, but it refers to all of the people of this nation as a group. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use the plural form of “mouth.” Alternate translation: [from the mouths of the people]

29.note: Cutting off one’s hair and throwing it away was a symbolic action by which people of this culture showed that they were mourning. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could explain the significance of this action in the text of your translation or in a footnote. Alternate translation: [In mourning, shear off your consecration hair]
The word **your** is singular here because Jeremiah is addressing the city of Jerusalem, so use the singular form in your translation if your language marks that distinction.

Jeremiah is using **lift up** as a common expression of the culture to mean “sing aloud.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and sing aloud a lamentation on the bare heights]

The **bare heights** are hilltops on which no trees grow. If your readers would not be familiar with what these are, you could use the name of a similar place that your readers would recognize, or you could use a more general term. Alternate translation: [the barren hilltops]

The terms **rejected** and **abandoned** mean similar things. Jeremiah is using the two terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [Yahweh has utterly rejected]

Jeremiah is using the possessive form to describe a **generation** that is characterized by **his fury**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the generation against which he is furious]

30.note: Jeremiah is speaking as if the people of Judah were the actual **sons** of a father named Judah. Alternate translation: [For the people of Judah] or [For the descendants of Judah]

Here, **their detestable things** represents the idols that these people worship. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [their detestable idols]
See how you translated the similar phrase in 7:10.

31.note: The words **Topheth** and **the Valley of the Son of Hinnom** are the names of places near Jerusalem.

Yahweh is using **it did not come into my heart** as a common expression of the culture to mean “I never thought of it.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and I never even thought of it]

32.note: Yahweh is using **days are coming** as a common expression of the culture to mean “a time is approaching.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [there will soon come a time]
The term translated as **Therefore** indicates that what follows is a result of what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes this clear. Alternate translation: [This is why]

Jeremiah is using the term **behold** to focus his listeners’ attention on what he is about to say. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation. Alternate translation: [pay attention, because days are coming]

32.q: וְ⁠לֹא יֵאָמֵ֨ר ע֤וֹד הַ⁠תֹּ֨פֶת֙ וְ⁠גֵ֣יא בֶן הִנֹּ֔ם
32.note: The expression **will no longer be called** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [and people will no longer call it Topheth or the Valley of the Son of Hinnom]

Yahweh is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [instead, it will be named the Valley of Slaughter]
The phrase **the Valley of Slaughter** is the name of a place.
The pronoun **they** refers to people in general rather than to any particular group. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [And people will bury in Topheth]

The implication is that so many people will die that there will be no room left to bury them anywhere else. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [because there will be no room to bury them anywhere else]

33.q: וְֽ⁠הָ֨יְתָ֜ה נִבְלַ֨ת הָ⁠עָ֤ם הַ⁠זֶּה֙ לְ⁠מַֽאֲכָ֔ל לְ⁠ע֥וֹף הַ⁠שָּׁמַ֖יִם וּ⁠לְ⁠בֶהֱמַ֣ת הָ⁠אָ֑רֶץ
33.note: The implication is that the bodies of these people will be left lying on the ground without being buried, which people of this culture considered a great disgrace. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [And the corpses of this people will be left unburied on the ground and will be for food for the birds of the skies and for the beasts of the earth]

Yahweh is not referring to a specific **bird** or a specific **beast**. He means birds and animals in general. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [for the birds of the skies and for the beasts of the earth]

The pronoun **them** refers to the corpses of the people of Judah, on which the birds and animals will be feeding. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [and there will be no one to scare away the birds and the animals]

34.q: וְ⁠הִשְׁבַּתִּ֣י מֵ⁠עָרֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֗ה וּ⁠מֵֽ⁠חֻצוֹת֙ יְר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם ק֤וֹל שָׂשׂוֹן֙ וְ⁠ק֣וֹל שִׂמְחָ֔ה ק֥וֹל חָתָ֖ן וְ⁠ק֣וֹל כַּלָּ֑ה
34.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you may want to put the information about what Yahweh will bring to an end before the information about the places where he will bring it to an end. Alternate translation: [And the sound of joy and the sound of gladness, the voice of the bridegroom and the voice of the bride, I shall cause to cease from the cities of Judah and from the streets of Jerusalem]

If your language does not use abstract nouns for the ideas of **joy** and **gladness**, you could express the same ideas in another way. Alternate translation: [the sound of people rejoicing and the sound of people being glad]

The terms **joy** and **gladness** mean similar things. Yahweh is using the two terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [the sound of great rejoicing]

Here, **the voice of the bridegroom and the voice of the bride** represents the celebrations that take place at weddings. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the sounds of wedding celebrations]
